utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, this is case number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Today we are Wednesday, the 4th of July 2007. I would like to greet the Prosecution representatives, Ms. Dahl in particular. I would like to greet Mr. Seselj, as well as all the people present in the courtroom who are helping us to do our job today. As you know, this is a Status Conference we are holding. This is the last Status Conference we are having before the summer recess. The next Status Conference will be held on Friday, the 17th of August, at 4.30 p.m. So please write this down. This will be held on Friday, the 17th of August, at 4.30 p.m. Now, as far as the following Status Conferences are concerned, we have a real issue with our schedule to make sure that we stick to our time because Courtroom I, II and III are going to be occupied because the trials are all ongoing, and for the time being, I cannot give you a hearing date because we have a very tight schedule. We could perhaps, during the month of September, set a date for our next Status Conference, or the other solution, if there is a possibility to hold it, or if this is not a satisfactory solution, however, I don't see how we could proceed otherwise, we could start a Status Conference at 8.00 in the morning and perhaps only hold it for 30 minutes because at 9.00, the trial in another case starts, and then resume the Status Conference on the next day at 8.00 and so on and so forth. I shall seize the Registry of this matter to make sure that we can have four hours in a continuum, but quite frankly, when I look at the schedule for the month of September, all the courtrooms are occupied because of the ongoing trials. This is a real conundrum for us so we will definitely try to come up with a solution. As soon as I have one, I will let you know. I am available, I can even hold a Status Conference in the evening. In my previous jobs I sometimes worked up until 4.00 and 5.00 in the morning. I know that this is not customary here but if we need to meet up, in that case, we will have to hold a Status Conference after 7.00. There are moments in life when one needs to adjust. There are seven trials ongoing at the moment, and obviously the courtrooms are overbooked, which does have consequences on the pre-trial stage of other trials. The Registry is currently looking into the matter. I cannot take a decision on this and state that a Status Conference will be held at 7.00 at night or 4.00 in the morning. I can do it on a personal basis. You may not be able to, Mr. Seselj, but I think you told me last time that were you an early bird and that you could be here in the early hours of the morning but for the moment, I don't know what our administration will tell us. Now, for the time being in September, I cannot give you the date of a Status Conference, unless we hold Status Conferences at 8.00 in the morning, which has already been the case in the past. I shall now address another important matter, namely the date of commencement of trial. The commencement of trial does depend on a number of factors which I shall come back to at a later stage. Now, insofar as we are able to find a solution to these issues, I told you at our last Status Conference that because of administrative problems, our administration had let me know that this trial could begin in November. So what is needed for a trial? A judge; B, a registrar; C, legal officers; D, interpreters, and therefore this requires a number of people. The staff for the moment is currently working on the Dragomir Milosevic case but as far as I know the Dragomir Milosevic case should end very soon, which means that we will be able to draw on these other resources and begin our trial, all the more that Mr. Seselj is in pre-trial detention and the parliamentary assembly of the Council of Europe has addressed this issue, in deliberation number 1564, has asked the Tribunal to set a date for the beginning of this trial, as soon as possible. So notwithstanding these deliberations, which I am not involved in, however I know that Mr. Seselj should be tried as soon as possible, given that he is in detention for a number of years now and that this situation has to come to an end. Therefore, the best time possible would be as follows: We could, on the 6th of November, hold the Pre-Trial Conference, the 6th of November is a Tuesday. Wednesday, the 7th of November, we would have the -- hear the Prosecution case and on the 8th of November, if Mr. Seselj would like to take the floor, he will take the floor if he so wishes on the 8th of November. Therefore, the first witnesses could come to testify on the following week, as of the -- as of Tuesday, the 13th of November. As you know, at Mr. Seselj's request and at my request also, we should be able to have a three-day-a-week trial. Ms. Dahl, now so that we are clear about all of this, I could, if need be, hand down an order. I would like to know what the Prosecution schedule looks like. I would like to know what the picture looks like regarding all your witnesses, all the witnesses you intend to call to testify in support of your case. Therefore, you should be able to draw up a schedule that would start on the 13th of November, 13th, 14th and 15th, and so on and so forth, and you write in the name of the witnesses, from the beginning of your case to the end of your case. In addition, I need to determine, pursuant to Rule 65 ter, the definitive list of your -- the final witness list and the length of their testimony. Your list should, therefore, mention the name of the witnesses, the time you intend to spend examining these witnesses. But I would also like to ask the Prosecution to call these witnesses in a logical order, from a judicial standpoint. It could look like this. I purposefully use the conditional tense because what I have in mind is also the issue of equality of arms and the Defence of Mr. Seselj who is representing himself, who also needs to prepare his defence. Therefore, but this is something I have already mentioned, but I shall say it again, in an ideal situation, you should start off with crime-base witnesses, i.e., the witnesses who will come to talk about what happened in the various municipalities. In the indictment, several municipalities are mentioned, and in that case, you call them to come to testify, to talk about these municipalities, in a consistent fashion. You bring together the witnesses that come to talk about a particular municipality, and then again another municipality. For instance, take the case of the larger area of Sarajevo and Mostar so you bring all the witnesses together who come to talk about the same municipality, so that the Judges, Mr. Seselj and the people who are listening to us get a clear vision of what actually happened in one or other municipality. So it's not a good idea to bring a witness who is going to talk about one particular municipality and then the next day witnesses going to be talking about another municipality, then it is very difficult to understand what is happening. So it's better to work along these lines. I think this is common legal practice. So this will also be beneficial to Mr. Seselj, who will be able to prepare his defence. Now, after that, we could proceed in the following manner. Crimes have been committed, facts have been stated, so we need to understand who committed these facts. So you should then call witnesses who will address this matter, in order to establish a connection between the facts and the perpetrators of these facts. It is important to target your witnesses appropriately, the witnesses who are going to come and talk about these matters. And at the end, you should call the witnesses who are going to be talking about the responsibility of the accused, so that we have a proper logical order, because in some trials, one witness is a crime-base witness and the next day we hear an international witness who is coming to talk about something else and then on the next day after that, another witness comes to talk about another subject, which with my French, logical mind, always defeats me somewhat. Then it is much better to proceed this way, like that. You understand what is what. Now, the reason I'm saying this is that the Prosecution has filed a number of motions with a view to admitting transcripts in other trials of 92 bis articles and various statements, and for the time being, I have not ruled on these matters because I felt it was for the Chamber to decide, but my personal view on this matter is the following: These applications, as far as I'm concerned, can only be assessed in light of the testimony of viva voce witnesses who will have already testified. Let me give you a very clear example, which is Rule 92 bis, which, as you know, Rule 92 bis should only corroborate existing material. The accused can always challenge this and say he wants to cross-examine the witness. This is one of the rights of the accused. But for the Chamber to be able to purposefully rule on a 92 bis rule motion relating to a witness who has been a victim, who is going to confirm what another viva voce witness has already said concerning a particular municipality, the -- it is important that the viva voce witness be heard beforehand. Let me say that the Chamber has to get the overall picture to be able to do this because, Ms. Dahl, when you ask us now to admit a 92 bis statement, whereas I know nothing about what might have happened because to date I have seen no document whatsoever, now, in order to rule on this, I need to hear a viva voce witness beforehand. Let me take the case of a witness who is going to come to talk about Mostar, and then you would like to adduce a 92 bis statement, a witness statements, which are going to confirm what another witness has already said about Mostar but I can't, at the outset state that I accept a 92 bis statement when nobody has come to talk about it yet. I think this would be inconsistent. Therefore, it is important that you give us your witness list and that the witness order follows a particular logic so that the Bench gets the overall picture of the way in which the Prosecution is going to present its case. You, of course, are entitled to present your case whichever way you deem right, but, of course, this has to be in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, but the Bench does control the way in which the witnesses are being called and the Bench must set the length of the trial. Now, in order to set dates, I need to have sufficient information and I need to have your schedule and I need to have your list of witnesses and the order in which you're going to be calling these witnesses. This should be disclosed to me as soon as possible, to enable me to set the time limits. When the trial had started in November, I recollect that the time set for the trial had been six months for the Prosecution and six months for the Defence. Maybe six months is the right amount of time. I honestly don't know. Much will depend on the schedule you are going to give me. And for the time being, I cannot tell you whether it's going to be six months, eight months, ten months, five months. I simply don't know, because I do not have the right information yet. So it is most important to have this schedule and list, and this is why I am making such a point of it. In addition, before addressing in a contradictory fashion the status of pending motions, I would like to say the following. The difficulties that have arisen from this trial, we would like to settle as quickly as possible. The difficulties were due to three factors mainly: A, the fact that the accused wanted to represent himself. This matter has been settled because the accused shall now represent himself, shall put his questions and will be in full control of his Defence case. B, a factor which was preventing the trial from starting was due to the question of documents, disclosure of documents pursuant to Rule 66 and 68. Mr. Seselj felt that he should receive all these documents in his own language. I have previously ruled on the matter upholding this because, as a Judge, I felt that an accused should receive all the documents in his own language when these documents are in support of the indictment, whatever the jurisdiction or country are. That's the least one can do. I have therefore ruled on the issue. To my surprise, the Prosecution then seized the Chamber, in its entirety, to ask for this decision to be reconsidered. Pursuant to Rule 73, I was given authority in the matter, and Chamber III ruled that this was within my competence, so I did not quite understand why the Prosecution proceeded this way. So this decision is final. Mr. Seselj should get all the documents in his language, pursuant to Rules 66 and 68. That was the second obstacle standing in the way of the commencement of trial. C, this is the last obstacle, and I hope that this one will also be lifted, this concerns facilities which should be granted to Mr. Seselj so that he can defend himself. He has filed a motion. The Prosecution has filed its brief, and the Prosecution has also made written submissions. Mr. Seselj, regarding this fundamental issue, as everybody can well imagine, the brief is several pages long and is currently being translated. I have been told that you will be getting the translation of this brief in your own language on the 20th of July. Why will you be getting it on the 20th of July? Because it takes time. The brief is a 26-page brief. It is in English and I'm sure it has already been disclosed to you or at least your associates, I'm sure, have it already but it makes sense that you have it in your own language. Therefore, if you would like to respond to this brief, pursuant to our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, you have seven days to do so. So you should provide your response before the 27th of July so that by the end of July, or the beginning of August, I can hand down a decision on this matter. My decision will, of course, take into account the -- your arguments, the argument as provided by both parties, but this is something I have already mentioned and it is no secret: You are entitled to legal aid, to assistance and you can work with associates, your associates must be paid by the Tribunal. In addition, you should indicate to the Registrar that you are unable to pay the fees of your associates and you should be managing your associates personally. It's for you to decide who is to work with you and at what time, and to avoid any particular problem, it would be better if on your team there would be at least one legal assistant that would meet the legal requirements of our Rule 45 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. In the decision I will hand down, I will stipulate, without stating that this is in any way compelling, I shall indicate that this would be a good way of proceeding. In a situation like yours, your team of associates should, as far as I'm concerned, be made up of at least one person who will be in contact with the Registrar, the legal officer, the Prosecution, and therefore this person will brief you on various matters, pending matters, solutions that have been found, and as a manner of speaking, this person would act as a go-between, between you and the Tribunal. So this person can fulfil the requirements under Rule 45. It's up to you to make sure they do, not mine. Regarding the people who are going to assist you at the hearing in court, who will be sitting next to you, if you so wish of course, if you do not wish to have them, it's up to you, these people, of course, we need to have interpreters working in the three languages, one of your associates at least should speak English, know English. Why so? Because you see, as I'm speaking, you have in front of you the translation into English of what I'm saying on the screen. You yourself may well know English, but it's impossible for you to be riveted to the screen at all times whilst listening to the witness, whilst listening to the Prosecutor, or whilst looking at the judges. So if, on the screen, there is a mistake or if you have a translation in English that does not quite correspond to the statement by the witness in B/C/S, then your assistant can tell you that there is a problem because on page so much, page 25, line 14, there -- this is being said in English but this does not fit what the witness said in B/C/S. So then you can ask for a change because there would have been a mistake in the translation. This is the reason why you need some help. Since you are alone, it's impossible for you to look, listen, check your documents whilst checking the screen as well. Hence, the need to have somebody next to you doing that job. Also, you might need a case manager, somebody who is going to help you physically with documents or making photocopies, preparing files, but also in court, if you intend to show a video clip, say and you have that clip, who is going to start the clip? Well, your case manager will. He or she will be the one doing it, launching the video clip so you need somebody to help you in your physical task because in court you may need to have their help. So this is what I'm going to state in the decision but, of course, you have to decide yourself. You will make up your team but my experience shows me that you need such help indeed. When an accused is assisted by a lawyer, you have seen this already, sometimes the accused has two counsel, lead counsel and the co-counsel. Then a third person on the team. So actually, when you have an accused who is represented by counsel, the accused has the help of three people. But here, in the instant case, you will alone so you need to have people helping you out. Do as you please, of course, but think it over, because these are material necessities making it difficult for you to be on your own without anybody helping you. Therefore, in my decision, I will set out the principle which is that you need to have a team made up of associates who will be paid by the Tribunal. The sooner the better. Indeed, if we do stick to the date of the 6th of November, your associates should be able to attend the hearing to help you purposefully. Before I move on to other issues, I am going to give you the floor, Mr. Seselj, and then I'll give the floor to the Prosecution. Let's start with Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may ask first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: At the last Status Conference, there was perhaps a potential for misunderstanding regarding the identification of persons by name and the question of whether that would violate protective measures that are in place and I would like to request an instruction and a ruling from you that if it is necessary for Mr. Seselj to refer to individuals by proper name that we move immediately into private session, therefore we will avoid misunderstandings regarding disclosure or inadvertent publicity that would be a violation of the rules of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm going to give the floor to you straight away, Mr. Seselj but I'd like to settle this matter, but you will be free of course to speak to this topic as well. Yes, the issue of disclosure of names. We have rules that say that certain witnesses should be granted protective measures. Therefore, there are several individuals who might testify and they have already or will be granted protective measures. As a result, you, when you mention a topic, whatever it may be, you might give the name of a witness because you did not know that that witness had been granted protective measures or because you didn't think of it on the spur of the moment or for any other reason, and then you see the name of the witness on the screen. I do not know personally the names of protected witnesses. If you say Mr. Popovic, I don't know whether Mr. Popovic is a protected witness or not. I do not know it at all. In order to avoid this type of problem, it might be best for you not to mention the name but for you to say Mr. X without giving his name because if you do not mention the name and it later on appears that the person is a protected witness, we have to sort of start security measures. They do exist. I have mentioned them expressly in an order. We can then redact the name and you know that we have a delay of 30 minutes to do so, but if there is a name in the transcript and nobody reacts and if we later find out that this said Mr. Popovic was some protected witness, I say Popovic, I could have said Mr. Smith, it's just a name I am using to illustrate what I mean, so if two weeks later we discover that this Mr. Popovic was a protected witness, then I will have to issue an order for his name to be redacted. But at some times the court deputy, of course, must endeavour to check that the names are not the names of protected witness. Same obligation for the Prosecution, but in spite of all these checks and balances, it happens that the name remains in the transcript and then the best thing for you to do, Mr. Seselj, is that of your own accord, you ask to move to private session because you're going to mention somebody who, as far as you know, is a protected witness and we'll move into private session or if you have a doubt, don't mention the name of that individual. So this is in order to protect witnesses. Yes, Ms. Dahl? Did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is a second aspect to the request. I wish to prevent there from arising an accusation that Mr. Seselj is fishing for information to which he is not privy, and apart from protecting the identity of witnesses, there are of course as Mr. Seselj knows witnesses whose identity has been concealed from him as a matter of security and we do not wish there to be an unfortunate problem where the post hoc redaction of the transcript signals to Mr. Seselj that he has uncovered the identity of witnesses who have not been disclosed to him pursuant to an order of the Tribunal delaying disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Regarding this second aspect, I must say it's a very complex one. As part of the preparation of his defence, I guess that Mr. Seselj, and he will say so himself later, he must have listed a number of individuals who in his mind might be useful to him, for his defence. So maybe that's what he has in mind. So he may have thought that certain individuals might potentially be relevant witnesses in order to highlight parts of his case. Then, spontaneously he might say, "Well, I have these names, these witnesses, X, Y, Z," but it might be that the witnesses he mentioned fall under your category or list of Prosecution witnesses that he's not aware of. That could happen. It could happen, because at times -- you know there is a certain fiction about Prosecution and Defence witnesses, this is a forensic fiction because actually these are witnesses of the Court, of justice as such, because as soon as they take an oath, they testify for the sake of justice. But we have witnesses who are called by the Prosecution in support of their case and we have Defence witnesses being called for the Defence case, but it may happen that you have witnesses who could go both ways, and then the Defence may feel that the said one witness is their witness, whilst you called him as a Prosecution witness so this is a very difficult case to solve. I'm not aware of Mr. Seselj's witnesses list. As to yours, you have numbers and names but it doesn't say anything to me because I am not informed of the material they are going to testify to. All this is going to be revealed in court. So you raise a problem, indeed, but the solution, the practical solution, thereof, is hard to find because you think that maybe in doing so, Mr. Seselj is going to be fishing for witnesses that he doesn't know the names of. So there we are treading into speculation territory. This may be founded, but it could also be totally wrong, and I do not have any ready-made recipe to prevent that. The only ready-made recipe would be to say to Mr. Seselj do not give names. That might be a good solution. So, Mr. Seselj, regarding all of the points I have mentioned so far, you wanted to take the floor and you have it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, perhaps I'm not going to take things in the same order. First I'd like to say a few words about the last point that the Prosecutor spoke about. I am duty-bound to protect the names of protected witnesses disclosed to me by the Prosecution. It is not my duty not to mention any name whatsoever fearful that it may be protected. Last time an embarrassing thing happened. I mentioned at the Status Conference the name of a witness who testified in public in a trial in The Hague. I assumed that he could appear in my trial as well. After the Prosecutor intervened, the Registry redacted that name from the transcript and the recording with the explanation that this witness was a protected witness in yet a third trial. So in one trial he appeared here. She appeared as a protected witness in another one, as an unprotected witness, but I have not been informed about anything yet. That is a situation for which the Prosecution can be blamed, not me. I'm not mentioning any names now, please don't let the Prosecutor interrupt me. I have never interrupted counsel for the Prosecution so don't let her interrupt me either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... finish and then you can respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: This is a matter of courtroom decorum. I would request that you ask Mr. Seselj to lower his voice. It appears as if he is yelling based on the volume and tone of his voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, last time I'd asked you while you spoke so loudly and you said that you were used to speaking loudly because you had been a teacher, professor at university, and as a politician you were used to speaking loudly. Would you mind sort of lowering your voice, the tone of your voice? Could you try?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, only if I move the microphone a bit further off. I don't see how I can turn the volume of my voice down. At one point I can speak softly, you see, but not throughout my discourse. I cannot think about that all the time. At one point in time, I will have to start to speak naturally. Right now, I've been speaking softly but when I focus on the essence, I'm going to talk the way I speak naturally. Your technicians should have the possibility of reducing the volume in the microphone and in this way, they can resolve the problem. You see, this is what Geoffrey Nice did too when I testified in the Slobodan Milosevic case. You know, this is mistreatment in order to avoid a debate about the essence. I started talking about the very essence and substance and then the Prosecutor, the counsel for the Prosecution, does not like the tone of my voice. She can get a different headset. She can have different ear phones that can eliminate all other background noise from the courtroom and then she can only hear the voice of the interpreter, whatever she wants to hear. You know if I did that intentionally, it would be impossible for a person to do that, to speak in a strong voice all the time. This is my natural voice. This is a God-given thing, just as God bestowed beauty on the counsel for the Prosecution, God bestowed this kind of voice on me so allow me to say what it is that I'm saying without interrupting me so, Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj. Ms. Dahl? You got an answer from Mr. Seselj, if his tone is too strong, the Registry could see to it that the volume is turned down. Technically I believe it's possible and that might be a solution to this problem. It is true that Mr. Seselj has been speaking in this way for a very long time, and as he explains, he can't focus on what he wants to say by -- and try to lower the volume. Because if he does so, he loses his train of thought. So that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand his explanation and respectfully I think that there has been a misunderstanding. It is not a matter of amplification through the sound system. It is a matter of Mr. Seselj modulating his own voice himself, because that is what is coming across the courtroom, and this is a small courtroom and I think this is an important matter for preparation for conducting the trial. Because if the reasonable observer perceives that Mr. Seselj is using what I would consider an outdoor voice and is yelling at the participants in this trial, there will be misunderstandings and interruptions to request him to please modulate the volume that he produces naturally. The other point I wanted to make is that as a matter of courtroom practice, objections by counsel are received not as intentional interruptions by the opposing party but a matter of courtesy. If I stand it is because there is an important point that needs to be made and courtroom decorum requires that we take turns and not take interruptions personally as a -- with the malicious intent to interrupt or thwart Mr. Seselj's opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, in this respect, the Prosecution is telling us that we are in a small courtroom but it's the largest because Courtroom II is much smaller. Courtroom I is also smaller. We are in the largest courtroom. The Prosecution are telling us that we are not in a large space, in an amphitheatre; therefore the decibel level uttered by someone in a small space can be tantamount to a sort of excessive volume. This is food for thought but go on, please, as to the merits of what you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Judge, whether you know the name of the late Russian general, Lebed. At one point he was candidate for president. He ran against Boris Yeltsin in the elections in 1996. As far as I can remember, and I think he got killed in a traffic accidents. I don't know if you've heard of him. I assume you have. And I don't know whether you heard the way he spoke. Could you imagine General Lebed appearing in this courtroom and his voice was far stronger than mine. How would he resolve that problem? The counsel for the Prosecution could not have said anything more nonsensical than what she said a few moments ago. It is malicious. My voice can be isolated for all of those present in the courtroom with better ear phones or better technicians running the equipment, and please don't trouble me with that any more. I cannot speak in an unnatural voice in the courtroom. I cannot speak differently from what I speak like in any normal conversation. It is impossible to ask me to do that. You have now succeeded in drawing my attention to something else and I assume that that's what you'll be doing throughout the proceedings because you'll be bothered by my voice and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I want to be protected from --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again she is interrupting me. That is impermissible, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objections are admissible when they are founded. Mr. Seselj has just provided an explanation, his explanation. You have provided yours. I will discuss the matter with the Registry to see whether it's possible to turn down the level because when you hear Mr. Seselj, you hear him in your own language as the way I do in my own language so if we can turn down the volume, we'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I do not have a solution right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You're misunderstanding the nature of my objection. I want to put on the record that Mr. Seselj turned his body towards me and began addressing me rather than the Court. That is a breach of the decorum of court rules. Arguments and submissions and discussions are with the Court and not across the aisle between the parties and I wish Mr. Seselj to be instructed by the Court that he should refrain from addressing the Prosecution directly, that he should make his discussions directly to the Judge and that he should refrain from making insults to insinuate baseless accusations such as malicious intent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, Ms. Dahl, he did not insult anybody. Do not relapse into mistakes in the past where the Prosecution wanted to say that Mr. Seselj was crazy, initiated proceedings saying that he was insulting people. I'm not going to fall into that trap that you are preparing for me. Mr. Seselj has given a technical explanation as to why he has a loud voice. There may be a technical solution to it. However, you are right in that we have here a discussion in court between -- it's a triangular thing. The parties address the Court, not the other party across the well. So of course when you answer me, Mr. Seselj, you have to look at me, because when you answer me, the Prosecution is not concerned but Ms. Dahl, I do insist rather heavily on this. In the courtroom, we must have peaceful proceedings. One or the other party should not address the other party because this does not contribute to a peaceful and serene examination of the case. We were dealing with technical matters right now, and Mr. Seselj is going to provide a technical answer to the issues he wanted to deal with. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I am addressing you only and you can see that from all the transcripts to date. However, it is my rhetoric freedom, how I'm going to express a particular thought. In principle, when witnesses appear here, either Prosecution witnesses or Defence witnesses, I will again put questions to them through the Court, addressing the Court I put a question to them, but then of course as a question of rhetoric freedom, it may seem that I'm addressing them directly. Secondly, as I address you I am conveying a certain message to the Prosecution and now the Prosecution is suffering because of this strong message and is trying to devalue it by showing that they do not know the rules of procedure and that by presenting some objections that are totally baseless. May I please move on to the merit now because this senseless discussion has been going on for 15 minutes now and I did not cause it in any way, it is only the malice of the counsel for the Prosecution that caused it. If you allow me now I'm going to move on to speak about the problems as you presented them. Judge, the Council of Europe is not a relevant international organisation that has the rights to submit any requests to this international court. They are bringing political pressure to bear because their objective is to have me convicted as soon as possible and to be eliminated as a political phenomenon on this planet. Those are their motives and that is why they mentioned my name in the resolution that you referred to. I call upon you as the Pre-Trial Judge, to make a public statement in which you will reject with indignation that part of the resolution of the Council of Europe because it is not your fault that my trial is running so late. From the moment when you took over this case, there was not a single delay that was caused by you. Irreparable harm has already been made to me because my trial did not start at a reasonable point in time. Now, I'm opposing any attempt that, due to political pressures of the Council of Europe, my trial starts before all the prerequisites are met. You know full well that all the trial requirements have not been met. I think that the 6th of November is an unrealistic date for the start of trial. Why is it so? At the last Status Conference you told me that the Trial Chamber allowed me to object to the reduced indictment and the expanded indictment. It's going to be a single document and you told me that I will have a month to do that. I still haven't received the documents in the Serbian language, so that one month has not started running yet. If I were to receive it today, my deadline for filing would be the 3rd or 4th of August. Then I assume that at least a month will be needed for the Trial Chamber to rule on my objections, because I will first and foremost challenge the jurisdiction of this Court to try violations that could be called hate speech and I will have the right to appeal once you decide. You know that as far as challenging jurisdictions appeal, I can appeal straight away without requesting certification to appeal from the Trial Chamber. The Appeals Chamber will probably need three months to decide on that. It is only then that it is possible to start the trial. Therefore, for this reason, the date of the 6th of November is unrealistic. It is also unrealistic for a more important reason. I will still not received the pre-trial brief, the revised list of witnesses and the revised list of exhibits. Allegedly they have compiled this in the English language. The other day they tried to have this handed over to me in the English language. I refused. Now the question is how much time they will need to have this translated. You yourself said that your translators translate four pages a day. When I'm going to receive all of this is a big question. Then in the request to re-examine your decision on the mode of discovery, the Prosecution itself admitted that they still have to disclose about 400.000 pages of material to me according to Rule 66 and Rule 68. You have that information on the footnote on the last page of the said document. 400.000 pages. Now, they say that they have a financial problem, that they need 75.000 euro to finance this but how many days do they need to do this? To get part of this material translated into Serbian and the part that is in audio form transmitted to paper? Once they have done all of that, how many days do I need to read all of this? 400.000 pages? If I'm to read 400 pages per day, on the condition that I read 25 hours a day, if I were to get up an hour earlier as some of my friends would tend to joke, I will need a thousand days. Without these thousand days, I cannot be trial ready. Of course, there is a remedy, a remedy lies in reduction, reduction of the material. According to Rule 66, reducing the number of witnesses, counts in the indictment and everything else. However, I vehemently oppose every attempt to reduce the discovery of according to Rule 68 because my inalienable right according to the rules to have the Prosecution submit to me all the documents for which at any point in time any one from the Prosecution assumed that they could be exculpatory. That is the 206.000 pages that I referred to the last time and the other time before that. 206.000 pages of exculpatory material. They have to submit that to me. And I have to have time to read this material, at least once, at least once. And you see how many days that boils down to. It is absolutely impossible for the trial to start on the 6th of November. I've been waiting for four and a half years. I'll wait another four and a half years but I'm not going to give up on any one of my trial-based rights. In the best possible case, the trial can start in the beginning of 2008 and as it has to end by the 31st of December 2008 it is impossible for the Prosecution to have six months to present their case. They can have three or four months and then the requisite is that I have to be given the same amount of time and you know that there has to be a break between the Prosecution case and the Defence case, and in that break I'm going to prepare the Defence witnesses. So 3.000 -- three months to them, three months to me, a three month break in between our two cases, there you are, nine months on the condition that the trial starts in March. It is impossible for it to start earlier. It can start earlier on the condition that I do not get all the material according to Rule 66, if I do not get all the material according to Rule 68 and also, to rush the trial as the Council of Europe would want to have things done because what matters to them is that I am convicted. They don't care about how I'm going to be tried. Not a single Western power cares about how I'm going to be tried; the Americans, the European Union, the entire NATO alliance, the only thing that matters to them is that I should be convicted. And that is why they are going to continue with their political pressure on the Court as they have been doing so far, and I am calling upon to you resist this political pressure because you have very strong arguments and you have not violated my trial and procedural rights a single time so far, and I am truly grateful to you for that. Some other matters have been referred to here, questions of financing. In this domain nothing has been done yet. This is a requirement that has to be met before the trial starts. I've already told you I'm not going to bring into question the beginning of the trial because the question of finance is not being resolved. And if -- even if my request to have my defence partially funded is rejected, I am not going to oppose the beginning of the trial. So money is not going to be an impediment but timely disclosure according to Rule 66 and 68 will be an impediment. I will not go to trial without that. If this disclosure is not carried out the trial cannot begin. The Prosecution can say that first they are going to disclose material for some witnesses according to Rule 66 and then subsequently for others. But they cannot say that for Rule 68, because all Rule 68 material is something that I have to have before the trial starts. Why do I need Rule 68 material once it -- the trial starts? If I cannot use that to cross-examine the Prosecution witnesses? I don't need the material later. I have to have all of this in a timely fashion before the first Prosecution witness appears here. All the Rule 68 material. Because it's not for the Prosecution to carry out a selection of this material and to say that I'm going to need this and I'm not going to need that. I'm the only one who can carry out this selection. For me it is important that they have stated and confirmed to you in writing that there are 206.000 pages of exculpatory material so now counsel for the Prosecution cannot come up and say, not all of this is potentially exculpatory, we are going to reduce this to 100.000, 50.000 or 20.000 pages. That is impermissible. This directly violates my rights. They have to bring all 206.000 potentially exculpatory pages in Serbian on paper. Before this is done, a regular trial can not start. If the trial is going to be irregular, if it's going to be pro forma, if you're only going to have summary proceedings without giving me the right -- the possibility for the right kind of defence, then that is not possible. At the last Status Conference, the Prosecution objected to me that I'm trying-- they said that in one of their submissions, that I'm forcing them to carry out a reduction. Of course, it is in my interest to force them into reduction. It is not my fault that the trial is running late, almost five years at that. I was trial-ready on day 1. It is their fault. However, the requirement is that they meet the necessary requirements. I never did anything that delayed the beginning of the proceedings, except insisting on my procedural rights. I still insist on my procedural rights. If my procedural rights are brutally trampled upon by not disclosing all Rule 68 material to me, these 206.000 pages, or if there is an unjustified delay in terms of disclosing Rule 66 material, whose fault is that? It certainly cannot be my fault. As for my legal advisers, I consider that question to have been resolved. Three of my legal advisers have been registered here, all three of them have degrees in law. One of them is an attorney-at-law but he didn't even have to be an attorney-at-law. My main legal adviser is not an attorney-at-law and he turned out to be a more capable lawyer than all the lawyers that had appeared before this Court until now. You will see that on the basis of the motions that he wrote. About 90 of them were written by him because after a while I told my legal advisers that everyone of them should sign or rather everyone of them should put their names down, whoever drafted these motions. That is Zoran Krasic and no one can bring into question the fact that he is not a lawyer. I meet the requirements for Defence counsel. I'm a university professor of law. And that suffices. My Defence team has a lawyer who meets all the requirements, and that's me. The rest don't have to meet any of these prerequisites, they work on my instructions, my orders, my suggestions, and I first check whether they did their job properly and then I sign their motions and then send them on to you. So that question has been settled. They don't know the English language. I already told you once, Judge, that sufficient protection for me is that I will get videotapes every day with complete recordings of the proceedings of a given day. That is sufficient for me, that I have proof that something was said or that something was not said. And you may be exposed to the danger of an incorrect transcript and then you have to find someone in the Registry to check the transcript. I assume the transcripts have to be checked, that what is typed in here at the time does not stay that way, that somebody compares the recordings with the transcripts at the end of the day because if this is not done, the transcripts will be a disaster. I am not able to and I will not monitor the transcript. What matters to me is that the video recordings be delivered to me and that will be my proof that something was said or not said. That suffices. I cannot do the ICTY's work here and monitor the transcript. The transcripts are here for you. They will be left for history and it's up to you to see to them. Now we come to the last issue, and that is mentioning the names of protected witnesses. It would be in the interest of the Prosecution to disclose to me, as soon as possible, the names of all the protected witnesses and I guarantee that neither I nor the members of my team assisting me in my Defence will ever attempt to contact those protected witnesses in any way. Otherwise, a situation will arise where, searching for Defence witnesses, we might come across a protected Prosecution witness, that person would not tell us that he's already a Prosecution witness and might agree to testify for the Defence, and that name will be found on the list of Defence witnesses. The Prosecution will then complain that we are stealing their witnesses. That's not just a hypothesis, it's a realistic possibility. And that can be solved if the Prosecution immediately provides a list of all their protected witnesses because then I will know that I should not contact those people for any reason. Otherwise, I will be constantly declared guilty of things that are not my fault but are their fault. Let me remind you of something that happened in 2005. In a conversation with a friend of mine, I mentioned the name of a man about whom I had heard that he had been a false witness in another case. I won't mention any names, so don't worry. And then suddenly I am denied all communication for two months by phone with my advisers, family visits, even my mail, my official mail was not delivered, which contained some submissions, for the duration of that ban. They imposed a sanction on me without holding disciplinary proceedings beforehand. I had heard that somebody had been a false witness and I said, well, stop having any dealings with him. It's my right to speculate about some people. It was not a person whose name was disclosed to me by the Prosecution as a protected witness. Later on, the Prosecution said that that person would be a protected witness in my case. Well, now that I know that, I will never mention his name again. But if I don't know that somebody is a protected witness in my case, I can mention any name I know, any name I've heard of, I could mention somebody's name and you will immediately intervene and say no, no, you can't mention that name, he is a protected witness. Well, then, you are revealing to me that that person is a protected witness. I didn't know that before. So I have forced you to disclose to me the name of at least one protected witness before you had planned to, even though I have to suffer for two months in the Detention Unit by being denied all contacts. Two close relatives died in the course of those two months and I didn't know about it. I didn't know two of my relatives had died. These are then all the possibilities opened up by this manner of proceeding on the part of the Prosecution. There is no reason for the Prosecution not to disclose all those names right away. If they do, we will have fewer problems of this kind. As regards documents, something that has been happening on a regular basis for the last five years is happening again. The Prosecution is delivering to me witness statements, and there is a lot of confusion in this. Sometimes they deliver to me statements that have already been disclosed. I get, for example, one witness statement and I know for a fact that the same witness made several statements, which I haven't got yet. I get a statement from a potential witness and I know that that witness testified in other cases. I'll mention a name, Miroslav Deronjic, because he's not protected, and I have received only his statement but not his testimony in the Milosevic case and in some other cases I think it was Krajisnik but I'm not sure about that. So they give me crumbs. I think, Your Honour, you should rule that when they give me -- when they disclose to me something that pertains to a witness, they should give me the complete material pertaining to that witness, not piecemeal. If they have a hundred witnesses, then in the order in which these witnesses will be called in the courtroom, let them disclose to me the complete material, witness number 1, here's the complete material for witness number 1, all the statements he made, all his testimonies in other cases, if there are any and all the exhibits to be tendered through that witness. However, they are creating complete confusion. They are preparing hundreds of documents to be introduced along with the name of a witness who is deceased. They are preparing hundreds of documents that have nothing to do with my case. They are doing this in an automatic manner. I'm going to insist on something that has not been respected in other proceedings. I have the right to put at least one question to each Prosecution witness in connection with each exhibit tendered through that witness. I have to ask him has he ever seen a document? For example, Witness X appears and they say we want to tender 300 documents through this witness. I have to put at least 300 questions to that witness. Have you seen this document, have you seen this document, have you seen this document, have you seen this document? Otherwise, what is the basis for tendering those documents through that witness? It's a problem I have seen in other cases and I will not just let this be done in my case. Otherwise, you can have a truck-loads of documents being brought in. There is something else I've learned here and I'll finish with that. So far, the Prosecution has been quite -- in quite a lull. There has been a huge number of cases here, and large numbers of Defence counsel, whether Serb, Muslim or Croat, have appeared here and they have falsely signed statements that they speak English or French, whereas the vast majority of them don't actually speak those languages. They had documents in foreign languages which they never read or looked at, they may have searched through them, and then they appeared in the courtroom to defend their client, and the Prosecution has become complacent because of that situation. In my case, there is an accused defending himself, acting on his own behalf, and insisting on all his rights, refusing to waive any of his procedural rights and now nothing can be disclosed in English, nothing can be disclosed that is not on paper and the Prosecution has been doing nothing for almost four and a half years, and now they suddenly say that the Defence should finance this, should provide 75.000 euros to have transcripts put on paper, which are in audio form in the Serbian language or to pay for translation from English into Serbian. Now the Defence has to do this. It's expensive, they don't care how the Defence is going to finance this. No, it's up to them to do that. I've had a lot of costs. I've had three judgements in the Rwanda Tribunal translated into Serbian because I needed them because they are referring to them. I asked the Registry for this. Registry said they were not duty-bound to provide this. I asked them -- I asked the Rwanda Tribunal and they said that they were not duty-bound to do that. These are three judgements pertaining to genocide that dolus specialis is required that they publicly call for genocide. Something like Streicher in the Nuremberg proceedings. They are referring to this in my case in order to artificially introduce hate speech, and of course I need to have arguments to counter this and I will do that in my objection to the indictment. Dolus specialis being required for genocide cannot be transferred to my case where I made some speeches which contained hate speech and now they are attributing to me that I incited someone to kill or rape or murder somebody or burn down a religious building. Dolus specialis has to be proved. This was an expense that I had to bear. Then I had to have the expense of translating the entire Limaj judgement into Serbian because registry refused to have it translated into Serbian. And I need that judgement. Well, now it's been translated, I received it the other day, 400 pages. So my costs are enormous. I am in debt. I have huge debts. And so I cannot take upon myself the duties of the Prosecution. I have enough on my plate already. And I cannot, therefore, acquaint myself with the entire jurisprudence of this Tribunal, a vast number of decisions which might be relevant for me have not been disclosed to me. Maybe four or five such decisions have been disclosed to me, as have all the judgements that exist in Serbian. But I have not received all the judgements that exist before this Tribunal. All the ones that have been delivered to me in Serbian, I have already read, I've made good use of my time, whereas the Prosecution waited and bided their time, expecting that I would not be able to defend myself, that I would be defended by false counsel who would be acting on behalf of the Prosecution rather than on behalf of my defence and that they would have an easy job as they did in some other cases. But that will not happen. I will either defend myself or I will no longer be alive. I will not insult anyone in the courtroom, I will not cause any physical incidents, and they cannot prove that I'm crazy. Who is crazy? Those people are crazy who thought they could deprive me of my procedural rights. I hope you'll agree with me, Judge. It is they who have turned out to be crazy, not I, who have been defending my procedural rights. I may be madly courageous or madly able, but I'm not mad.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to object on put on the record again that Mr. Seselj is speaking --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're interrupting me again for no reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... and impugning the motives of the Prosecution without cause and I repeat my request that he be directed to address only the judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say anything to counsel, Your Honour, I was addressing only you, and I have not said anything that is offensive to the Prosecution. I said in principle that those people are crazy who thought they could deprive me of my procedural rights. I have the right to say that. It's not personal. I have not identified any persons. Now, one more point and I'll finish. There were several submissions filed by the Prosecution in June, where they wished to bring into question Your Honour's ruling that everything should be disclosed to me in Serbian and in writing, and also my criminal report and my request for a review and I have also seen the Prosecution reply, response, and they list a number of statements I made and things I did, and generally speaking they want to prove that I am a very bad man and that that is a reason to deprive me of my procedural rights. Let me tell you: I accept that I'm a bad man, not only a bad man but the worst man in the world. The fact that I'm accused of the most heinous war crimes shows that I'm a bad man. Of course, the Prosecution, part of the public, the Western powers all start from this viewpoint, but even if I were the worst man in the world, that would not be an argument to deprive me of a single procedural right, because procedural rights exist precisely to protect criminals, bad people, who are presumed innocent until proved guilty. So I accept that I am the worst person in the world but I refuse to have any of my procedural rights denied for that reason. I have rights on which I insist. Thank you for listening to me and hearing me out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, first of all, nobody wishes to deprive you of your rights, and I least of all. You do have rights. This has been acknowledged. And you should exercise your rights. If you're being deprived of your rights, there is no fair trial. In that case, you would be quite right to question those people who have deprived you of your rights. As I don't wish to deprive you of your rights, I shall -- I'm about to look into those important matters you have raised. A while ago, I indicated that the trial could start on the 6th of November. You gave your personal view on the matter which is very important and you expressed it in two ways. You first of all said that the indictment is challenged, I'm going to get back to this, and as far as you're concerned it would be difficult for you to start on the 6th of November. And you then addressed another item, which stands in the way of the commencement of trial, which is the issue of disclosure of material pursuant to Rule 68 and disclosure of 206.000 documents. Now, as far as the indictment is concerned, the situation has become even more complicated. Let me sum it up. The indictment, which was the support medium of the trial that was due to start on the 6th of November, the Trial Chamber has entitled you to file a preliminary motion. So, this was pending. But after that, the Prosecution on the 25th of June, namely a few days ago, has just filed a modified indictment, which I have before me, which contain a number of changes. Certain words have been taken out. Other words have been changed. And in paragraph 5 of the indictment, for instance, anything relating to the commission has been deleted. In paragraph -- in other words, paragraph 5 is now only a four-sentence long paragraph. As the indictment has been modified, you are entitled to file a preliminary motion. You have 30 days to do so, as soon as you have the new indictment in your own language, i.e., the modified, the amended indictment. I don't know whether you're aware of this but the Prosecution has applied the Brdjanin case law on this matter regarding JCE and the Prosecution has also done away with a number of things. So we now have two indictments. The first indictment was an indictment on which you filed preliminary motion and we now have a second amended indictment. In your written submissions, you may join the two indictments and file a preliminary motion on both the first and the second, but the second is just an extension of the first one, a modified version of it. Now, this starts running 30 days from the day you receive the indictment. You will have to respond. The Prosecution might file its response. The Trial Chamber will then hand down a decision, but as far as the indictment is concerned, I don't have full powers, because this falls within the competence of the Chamber in its entirety and the Chamber will have to hand down a decision on this. After that time, you will be able to ask or request certification to appeal. I think you mentioned this. I don't know. The Appeals Chamber will then have to rule on the matter. Given the time-line in question, I think we will not be able to start in November. But my working assumption, which started on the 6th of November, for the date of commencement of trial, was something which I didn't think would be challenged by the Appeals Chamber but you are of course entitled to seize the Appeals Chamber on this matter. So on the 6th of November, because of the question of the indictment, we might have to postpone the commencement of trial. The second issue which you mentioned, which I shall mention again when we resume after the break, we have to have a break for technical reasons, the question of the 206.000 pages which I shall address after the break. We have to adjourn for 20 minutes in order to change over the tapes and we shall resume again in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed. I am now going to address the second issue raised by Mr. Seselj in relation to Rule 68, exculpatory evidence. Mr. Seselj mentioned 206.000 pages. According to him, they are mentioned in the motion for reconsideration of the decision I had issued. Could the Prosecution enlighten me on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The problem identified by Mr. Seselj with regard to managing the information that is being disclosed to him on paper, I think highlights one of the difficulties of self-representation that comes with the exercise of that right. We are methodically reviewing all of the disclosure in the past in light of the recent decisions to ensure full and expedient compliance with our disclosure obligations. Each receipt that we provide to Mr. Seselj indicates the nature of the rule-based disclosure obligation being satisfied, that is we identify with specificity what portion of the rules the material falls within. We include an index of the material that gives a brief overview, and we trust that that will assist him in maintaining the organisational structure that serves his preparation needs as well as organises the material for preparation during -- for preparation for trial. I would note with regard to the items disclosed in the past in electronic form, under the name of Rule 68, that those receipts, and I'm speaking specifically about receipt number 10 from September 2004, do not differentiate the application of the rules as they are today. Rule 68 has five parts, and the rulings of this Chamber regarding Rule 68(i), that is material within the actual knowledge of the Prosecutor that may suggest innocence, mitigate guilt or affect the credibility of the Prosecution evidence, we are reviewing material -- we are reviewing the prior disclosure to determine whether it can be categorised. Presently the large volumes of material tendered in electronic form would appear to fall within sub-prong 2, and we are looking at the search terms that produced the search results that are included in those disks to determine whether or not they would be categorised under Rule 68(i). The material on disk represents the search results based on electronic rules, and represents an electronic collection tendered in that format for the purposes of searching for terms that can be located with the search engine. We will not print or translate materials on disk. The disclosure of material in electronic collection is dependent on the electronic qualities of the targets of the search and the efficacies of the search result. Since 2004, our evidence collection has been subjected to improvements in technology that allow the identification of search terms with more precision, and we will discharge our disclosure obligations under Rule 68(i) as material comes within our actual knowledge, and if the accused wishes to review in electronic form collections of relevant material that fall within Rule 68(ii) we will authenticate those available to him in electronic form. We reject his broad and general criticism about compliance. Our intention is to ensure a fair trial. I will not rush and make mistakes and give him material that is disorganised or unlabelled. I will make sure that the relevance of the material that is provided to him is plain and that we are scrupulous in disclosing material that is required under the rules and will serve his preparation of the defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, here are my comments to Rule 66 and 68. Rule 68 -- 66 gives you the obligation to disclose to Mr. Seselj, in his own language, all material which were used to draft the indictment. These are documents that were brought before the confirming judge, the judge who confirmed the indictment. Well, the accused must have them in B/C/S. That's a rule that is applicable to all because the indictment is constructed on material, and it is normal for the accused to be aware and to be informed of the material. The documents are going to be useful since you're going to have a witness list which is going to list the documents witness by witness. That's Rule 66(A)(i). Now, we have Rule 66(A)(ii). You are to provide Mr. Seselj with copies of witness statements which you intend to call to testify at trial, and copies of all transcripts and written statements further to Rule 92 bis, 92 ter and 92 quater. So he needs to have them too. Nobody can help this. Nobody can waive this. And he needs to have them in his own language. Now, as to Rule 66(B), at Mr. Seselj's request, you must allow him to inspect any books, documents, photographs and tangible objects in your custody or control which according to him are material to the preparation of his defence. But this can be done electronically.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: If I may interrupt, we had considered based on the prior Trial Chamber's rulings, that Mr. Seselj had made a request under Rule 66(B) for material mentioning witness testimony mentioning him by name. That's being done in paper for your information, so we have gone beyond simply providing access in electronic form. I don't -- I don't believe that he's made other specific requests triggering this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If you've done so, it's even better. Now, as to Rule 68, I sometimes find it difficult to know why we have this rule in the rules. 68(i): "The Prosecutor shall, as soon as practicable, disclose to the Defence any material which in the actual knowledge of the Prosecutor may suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence." We have two categories of documents. We have documents that may indeed suggest his innocence. He needs to have them and if he has them, this must cause the indictment to be amended. The other category is documents that might affect the credibility of other evidence. And he needs to have them too. He needs to have those documents in his own language. That's Rule 68(i). However, Rule 68(ii) says that: "The Prosecution shall make available to the defence, in electronic form, collections of relevant material held by the Prosecutor, together with appropriate computer software with which the defence can search such collections electronically." Let me take an example. It could be that in other cases, there may be links with the indictment against Mr. Seselj and you may think it might be useful for Mr. Seselj to have them. But then you convey that to him electronically and it's up to him to carry out the research. However, documents under Rule 68(i) have to be disclosed to him in his own language. At the latest Status Conference, I asked you to list very clearly all the documents that had been disclosed to him under Rule 66, and to check that the documents had at the very least been already listed in the Rule 65 ter list of exhibits and as far as the remainder of documents is concerned, that you do not plan to use, that he had them in your -- in his own language. That's Rule 66. I don't know what the documents are that fall under Rule 68. I don't need to know that because this is something between you and him. You are under the obligation, should you have a document, an exculpatory document, under the obligation of disclosing that to him. But the Chamber does not know at all what the document is. My concern is as follows. In order to prepare Mr. Seselj's trial, for him to have equality of arms and a fair trial, he needs to have made available to him documents that may be useful to his case. Based on that, I have several questions for you, Ms. Dahl. At the Status Conference on the 2nd of May, Mr. Seselj asked for transcripts of the meetings between the Prosecutor and Mr. David Hooper to be disclosed to him; was that done or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not aware of any transcripts of any meetings between the Prosecutor and Mr. Hooper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, look into this, please, because I'm going to put the question again to you on the 17th of August. Then there is the issue of the 38 binders. At the last Status Conference, I had suggested the following solution. I had asked you to draw a list of the documents that had been disclosed to O'Shea and Hooper under Rules 66 and 68, and based on that, that you should convey this to the Registry, which was going to look into the binders, take out of those binders the documents that were relevant, and send them to Mr. Seselj. My question is: Have you done this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have the list. It's several thousand pages long. It's in the form of an Excel spreadsheet. It includes reference to every single exhibit under the prior exhibit list numbering system, and we'll make that available to the Registrar on a disk format or on paper, whatever is most expedient for searching it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling me that this is several thousand pages long, line 23, page 42. This is what I'm reading. And you say that it is in the form of an Excel spreadsheet. Two questions. Well, now normally, you should be doing this, but the Registrar might do it. You need to have this printed out. And my other question is whether the documents have been translated into B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: With regard to the materials disclosed to prior counsel, they were disclosed as per the rules that applied to disclosing to prior counsel. We are making arrangements to ensure that all of the exhibits are made available to Mr. Seselj in paper and in Serbian, and we consider that the revised exhibit list that we filed last Monday should be the one that we work from because the renumbering eliminates the utility of the material that was loaded into e-court for preparation for last year's trial, and it eliminates or it creates -- it eliminates the utility of the material disclosed to prior counsel. I found in engaging in the work to renumber and declare relevance for all of our exhibits that I could not simply use the old list and rearrange the numbering, that it required going through each exhibit and we considered that the starting point to assist Mr. Seselj would be to use the current list so that he's not required to remap or rearrange old material that either exists only in English or has not been improved according to the current rulings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true, and I thank you for this, because I noticed that you had really done some titanic work, you had renumbered the documents, complying with my instructions, with, as number 1, the oldest document. From memory I think it's back to 1844. And then you ordered the documents accordingly. From memory I seem to remember that there are close to 6.000 documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. What I did to make sure that we had a numbering system that could adapt if leave were granted to add additional exhibits, is that I began with 1 and continued, all of the exhibits that are actually documents. We then segregated and started a new numbering series that grouped audio files, videotapes and other kinds of visual pieces of evidence together as well as listing separately, under a separate series of numbers in an abundance of caution, the witness statements that we have tendered as evidence under the rules, either the prior 89(F) or any of the permutations under the current Rule 92. And so the numbering system assists in finding material quickly by its relevant category. A lot of material was not dated and in different formats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As to the work you have done, what I'm asking, and I think that Mr. Seselj may ask a similar thing, I'm asking you to put all these documents in binders with numbers and to bring them to me, and if you do the same for Mr. Seselj, he will have available to him in his cell all the Prosecution documents in binders. So that he can immediately refer to the documents because everything will have been ordered. Of course, if there is a number referring to a videotape, well, he'll have the videotape as such, or on CD, he can look at it straight away. How long do you need to make the binders for the Pre-Trial Judge and for Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Well, I had inquired as to the production methodology and we are hoping to have all the exhibits uploaded or installed in an e-court module, and that gives us the facility to apply labels when we print out the physical documents. We thought it would be unwise to produce binders that did not have labels affixed to the document. I was afraid that if a binder fell off a table and the contents were scattered there would be no way practically to determine if it was Exhibit 1 or 2 or 3. So I want to have the labelling affixed. I'm hoping that the e-court work will be done by the end of next week and then we will be able to produce very efficiently the material in paper format in the order in which it's numbered and the material that is in disk format, of course, we will put with its numbers in pockets so that it can be maintained in an organised manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, this is what should be disclosed to you, because what you are going to have is what I'm going to have as well. Ms. Dahl has just explained to us that all the exhibits, of which you already have a list because it was done in English, I'll give you the floor in a minute, you should have this list. There are many documents, and Ms. Dahl is filing this or uploading this in the e-court system and once this is done, as soon as it is done, they are going to prepare binders for us with the numbers of -- the document numbers and on each document there will be a label with the e-court number. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I want to be sure that there is an understanding that there is -- there are a number of documents that we have requested in the context of the protective measures motion to have disclosure delayed and there are also a number of documents that are subject to restrictive conditions by the provider. Those -- that subset has been redacted so I've separated those out and we've foreseen the ability to add the documents in as ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, you have been listening to this. Do you have any comments on this issue, the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, first of all, I would like to draw your attention to the fact that there is a typographical error in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. For example in Rule 68, these are Roman numerals i, ii, iii, iv, v, not i, double i, triple i, as the interpreter has been interpreting for me. Obviously these are Roman numerals, and it's a typographical error, the fact that they were not typed out as Roman numerals. It's as if you could type out Roman numerals out that way, that is how they have been represented here. Now, why am I particularly referring to this? Because I want to be as accurate as possible in what I'm going to say just now. The Prosecutor is consciously saying something that is untrue. 206.000 pages of documents, according to Rule 68, pertain to 68(i), so these are materials which according to the actual knowledge of the Prosecutor may suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence. All 206.000 pages pertain to that. Now, the Prosecution is in trouble because they have to submit all of this in writing and in the Serbian language. Therefore, they want to reduce this in a concealed manner and to present it to you that way. They are trying to say that a lot of this is 68(ii) material, that this is a collection of relevant material and so on and so forth. They would like simply to eliminate a lot of these 206.000 pages or 260.000 pages. They -- all these pages pertain to 68 (i), and you will see that from the document that I invoked last time, the one from November, and I hope they will submit that to you. So no reduction can be carried out there, 206.000 pages are the documents for which the Prosecution stated at a given point in time that they could be potentially exculpatory material, and all of that has to be submitted to me, not only to a have small portion submitted to me and that I have to look through their collection of documents in electronic form. So this is evasion of their responsibility, their obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... I understood.
